name: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy Ltd
title: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy Ltd - 542760 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Record FY26 turnover INR 7,548 cr and UOV above INR 11,800 cr, but Q4 revenue fell to INR 1,946 cr as developers deferred ordering, and EPC margin guide held at 8-10%.

triggers.label: Q4 order inflow muted, shifted to Q1
triggers.quote: EPC ordering activities by developers in the fourth quarter was largely muted.

triggers.label: Q4 revenue drop from deferred supplies
triggers.quote: Company had to defer some of the supplies and revised the execution plans accordingly in Q4 FY26

triggers.label: Revenue growth ~15% targeted for FY27
triggers.quote: we'll definitely be growing at a reasonably, let's say, 15% I mean, growth, yes.

triggers.label: Gross margin on international EPC 13.2%
triggers.quote: margins reflated to 13.2% versus 8% in FY25

guidance.quote: we'll definitely be growing at a reasonably, let's say, 15% I mean, growth, yes.
we anticipate EPC gross margins to range between 8% to 10%, depending on whether they are turnkey or BOS orders.
On the O&M side, we expect the gross margin to stabilize at around 20% level.

red_flags.label: Open-ended US litigation exposure beyond INR200 cr
red_flags.quote: Could be more, in fact. We'll come back to you.

red_flags.label: Q4 margin spike from one-off savings
red_flags.quote: there were certain savings over the budgeted cost that has improved our overall margin

red_flags.label: Reliance order timing unclear
red_flags.quote: I will say no comment at this point.

evasions.topic: Reliance New Energy timing and margins
evasions.quote: So all terms and conditions, everything are yet to be decided, discussed. So at this moment, I can't tell you any number.
Since it is a court case -- we are not considering that we will be losing the case and therefore, no provision to be made at this stage.
It may not be happening in maybe this financial year.

summary.headline: FY26 revenue hit a record INR7,548 crore (+20% YoY) and Q4 PAT a record INR142 crore, but FY26 net loss of INR296 crore after INR611 crore exceptional litigation charges.
summary.overview: Management reported record FY26 turnover of INR7,548 crore, up 20% YoY, and record quarterly PAT of INR142 crore in Q4 FY26. Q4 revenue fell both sequentially and YoY to INR1,946 crore because commodity volatility forced deferral of some supplies and execution plans. FY26 order inflow was over INR10,000 crore (EPC inflow up 43% YoY to INR10,062 crore), taking unexecuted order value (UOV) to a record INR11,813 crore. Management guided to about 15% revenue and order growth in FY27 and excluded any Reliance New Energy orders from that view.

financial_highlights.change: after INR611 crore exceptional items (litigation, Q2 and Q3)

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 forex gain included in EBITDA

financial_highlights.change: vs negative INR407 crore in Q3

segments.name: Domestic EPC
segments.commentary: Domestic EPC revenue was INR5,836 crore in FY26; domestic UOV is about INR9,250 crore (78% of total). Domestic order inflow was 10 projects totalling 4.8 GW DC and INR7,659 crore, up about 30% in value.

segments.name: International EPC
segments.commentary: International revenue was INR1,444 crore in FY26 with UOV of about INR2,562 crore. Gross margin reached 13.2% in FY26 (vs 8% in FY25), helped by three projects commissioned under budgeted cost in Q4. Two South Africa projects were won for US$270 million.

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: Total O&M portfolio rose to 13.5 GW from 8.7 GW a year earlier. Management expects gross margin to stabilise around 20%; a roughly 900 MW O&M order from Serentica was won in Q4.

segments.name: Battery storage (BESS)
segments.commentary: FY26 included one pure BESS order of 790 MWh. About INR300 crore of current UOV is battery-related, and management expects about 20% of new orders to come from BESS, at 8-10% gross margin.

guidance_outlook: Revenue and order growth of about 15% in FY27, based on current UOV plus Q3 and Q4 order inflows; the figure is inclusive of battery, wind and solar, and excludes Reliance.
EPC gross margin expected at 8-10%, depending on turnkey vs BOS mix; O&M gross margin expected to stabilise around 20%.
Management cited an overhead range of 4-4.5% of revenue, implying an EBITDA margin of about 4-5%.
Reliance New Energy (Khavda) orders: management said this year 'should happen' but gave no timing for the quarter, and no margin or size guidance.
Nigeria project is slow due to elections and is unlikely to happen in FY27.
Overall bid pipeline is about 31 GW, of which India is more than 27 GW, with an opportunity of about INR55,000 crore. Management targets a market share of about 25%.
capex_capacity: Delivered and commissioned about 4.5 GW AC (about 5.9 GW DC) in FY26, roughly 15% of India's utility-scale solar commissioned in the year (28.3 GW AC per MNRE).
Employee headcount rose to about 3,500 from 2,500 a year earlier, to support multi-GW projects.
Coal India 1.2 GW DC turnkey project in Rajasthan (L1 declared, LOA pending); NTPC tender still awaited.
Adani/Khavda execution timeline is about 13 months; a project with NTP still pending runs 14-15 months.
Management expects some Rajasthan substation projects to be delayed by a few months, with 2028 as the point when grid connectivity clears.
demand_pricing: India installed solar crossed 150 GW; the last 50 GW took about 14 months versus 11 years for the first 50 GW.
Q4 FY26 EPC ordering was muted due to geopolitical tensions and commodity volatility. Management said orders slated for Q4 mostly shifted to Q1 FY27.
PV module prices have risen since January 2026 (China production cuts, removal of export tax credits from April 1). Management says existing orders have back-to-back pricing protection.
Historical hit ratio is about 25-28%; current solar market share is above 25%.
Turnkey was about 70% of FY26 orders, and about two-thirds of current UOV.
Over 50 GWh of battery opportunities are seen; MNRE reports point to about 60 GWh. Hybrid and standalone BESS are both being pursued.
Third-party O&M contracts run 2-3 years (some longer), with gross margins targeted at more than 20% in India.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Reliance New Energy orders start, and what are the margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said deep engagement continues on technology and configuration and that traction should come in FY27, but gave no timing for the quarter, no order size and no margins. Reliance is excluded from the 15% growth guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 FY26 margin improvement a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Ajit Pratap Singh said three international projects near completion delivered savings over budgeted cost; this is not a recurring margin level, and the 8-10% EPC guidance stands.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the exposure in the US litigation cases, and could the loss be larger than INR200 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The company has about INR200 crore out of pocket, largely backed by a promoter indemnity. Management could not quantify additional litigation or penalty costs if cases are lost, saying the outcome is expected to take about 2 years, and the chance of losing is 'very remote'.

qa_highlights.question: What is the likely order-win rate and market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Historical hit ratio is 25-28%, and market share in solar is above 25%. Management expects the market share to stay above 25%.

qa_highlights.question: What growth is implied by the order pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The pipeline is about INR55,000 crore; at a 25% share, order book would grow about 15% from current levels (close to INR14,000 crore by FY27 end if the analyst's assumption holds).

qa_highlights.question: Are there any upside claims from erstwhile promoters after the INR611 crore write-off?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR611 crore case was non-indemnified and fully paid by end Q4, so nothing is recoverable on it. Claims on other cases can be raised for liabilities crystallised by 30 September; about INR180 crore was paid in FY25.

qa_highlights.question: How will the bank rating and credit lines affect the business?
qa_highlights.answer: The company is rated BBB+, up two notches from BBB- at the start of the year. Fresh credit lines of about INR2,800 crore were raised and LC/BG costs have fallen.

risks_watch: Estimated US litigation: about INR200 crore cash out, mostly indemnified by promoters. Management did not rule out additional costs if the cases are lost; the timeline is about 2 years.
Reliance New Energy timing and margins remain undisclosed; management declined to commit.
Module and commodity price increases (silver, copper, aluminium) and Chinese export tax credit removal could squeeze margins on unprotected orders.
Q4 gross margin of the international EPC segment was helped by one-time savings; sustaining 13%+ margin is uncertain against the 8-10% guidance.
Rajasthan grid connectivity and substation delays could slow execution; over 40 GW of PPA-signed projects are waiting for connectivity.
Nigeria project is unlikely in FY27 due to elections.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order visibility, O&M growth and the FY27 15% growth target. Evasive on Reliance timing, margins and the quantum of US litigation exposure, where management declined to give a number beyond the INR200 crore already cash out.
key_quotes: So basically, it depends on a lot of factors.
Since it is under court, so it can take maybe 2 years because U.S. court, all of you are aware that it's taking much longer time.
We are out of money for around more than INR200 crores and that is predominantly backed by the promoters under indemnity agreement on the US cases.
So there's no question of taking any hit on this INR200 crores.

growth.why: Management guides about 15% revenue and order growth in FY27 (ex-Reliance), backed by UOV of INR11,813 crore plus Q3/Q4 order inflows; Q4 revenue fell to INR1,946 crore (down YoY and QoQ) on deferred supplies, and no new company-owned capacity was quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management held EPC gross margin guidance at 8-10% and said the Q4 international margin (13.2% FY26 vs 8% FY25) was helped by one-off savings on three projects, not a recurring level; operational EBITDA margin guided to about 4-5%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Guidance of about 15% revenue and order growth in FY27 is backed by UOV of INR11,813 crore (domestic about INR9,250 crore) plus Q3/Q4 order inflows, though Q4 FY26 revenue fell to INR1,946 crore on deferred supplies.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No new company-owned capacity was quantified; the company delivered 4.5 GW AC and grew headcount to about 3,500 to support execution, with no capex plan stated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is a new ~15% FY27 growth target, and management excluded Reliance New Energy orders from it; Reliance timing and margins remain undisclosed, so there is no clear upside signal.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 FY26 revenue fell to INR1,946 crore (down YoY and QoQ) on commodity-driven deferrals, module prices have risen since January 2026, and Rajasthan substation delays could slow execution, though back-to-back pricing protects existing orders.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Battery storage is a growth push: about INR300 crore of current UOV is battery-related and management expects about 20% of new orders from BESS at 8-10% gross margin, but only one pure BESS order (790 MWh) was won in FY26.

rows.label: Reliance New Energy (Khavda) orders
rows.why: Management said traction 'should' come in FY27 but gave no timing, size or margin, and Reliance is excluded from the 15% guidance.

rows.label: Coal India 1.2 GW DC and NTPC tender
rows.why: Coal India project is L1 declared with LOA pending and the NTPC tender is still awaited, against a bid pipeline of about 31 GW (India over 27 GW, about INR55,000 crore) and a 25% target share with a 25-28% historical hit ratio.

rows.label: US litigation exposure
rows.why: About INR200 crore is already cash out, mostly promoter-indemnified, and management could not quantify further costs if cases are lost, though it called the chance of losing 'very remote'.

tone.note: Management was confident on order visibility, O&M growth and the 15% FY27 growth target, but cautious and evasive on Reliance timing, margin sustainability and the size of US litigation exposure; analysts pressed on those points.
